title: HTML Source Code Comments Disclosure - Template Names Exposed
description: The HTML source code returned by the application contains HTML comments that reveal internal template structure and file names. Each HTML response includes comments like "<!-- templates/home.html -->", "<!-- templates/form.html -->", and "<!-- templates/base.html -->". These comments reveal the internal directory structure and template organization of the application. The vulnerability affects multiple endpoints including the home page (/) and the addbook page (/addbook).
impact: Information disclosure that aids attackers in understanding application architecture. The revealed template names and directory structure (/templates/) can help attackers: (1) understand the application's internal organization, (2) identify potential additional endpoints or functionality, (3) perform targeted attacks on template rendering engines, and (4) identify SSTI (Server-Side Template Injection) attack surfaces. While low severity individually, this information disclosure helps attackers build more sophisticated attack chains and increases reconnaissance effectiveness.
evidence:
POC execution confirmed the vulnerability across multiple endpoints:

1. GET http://localhost:5000/ returns HTML comment:
   <!-- templates/home.html -->

2. GET http://localhost:5000/addbook returns HTML comments:
   <!-- templates/base.html -->
   <!-- templates/form.html -->

POC Output:
```
=== HTML Comments Template Disclosure POC ===
Target: http://localhost:5000

--- Checking endpoint: / ---
✓ VULNERABILITY FOUND: HTML comments revealing template structure

Template comments found:
<!-- templates/home.html -->

--- Checking endpoint: /addbook ---
✓ VULNERABILITY FOUND: HTML comments revealing template structure

Template comments found:
<!-- templates/base.html -->
<!-- templates/form.html -->

=== RESULT: VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED ===
Application exposes internal template structure through HTML comments
```

The vulnerability is confirmed - the application embeds server-side template comments in HTML responses that should not be present in production.
remediation:
1. Remove all HTML comments from production templates that reveal internal structure - replace template-level comments with code-level comments in the source files

2. Implement a build/deployment process that strips comments from HTML in production builds using HTML minification tools

3. Configure the template engine to not output debugging comments:
   - In Flask/Jinja2, ensure debug comments are disabled in production
   - Use Jinja2 environment settings: strip_newlines=True, trim_blocks=True, lstrip_blocks=True
   - Example:
     ```python
     from jinja2 import Environment
     env = Environment(
         strip_newlines=True,
         trim_blocks=True,
         lstrip_blocks=True
     )
     ```

4. Use HTML minification in production builds (tools like htmlmin, grunt-contrib-htmlmin)

5. Disable debug mode in production Flask application (DEBUG=False)

6. Implement Content-Security-Policy headers to limit information extraction vectors

7. Perform regular code reviews to ensure no sensitive information is embedded in HTML comments
references: OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control (Information Disclosure), CWE-200 - Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor, CWE-540 - Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code
toolCallDescription: Documenting HTML source code comments disclosure vulnerability with confirmed working POC that demonstrates template names are exposed in application responses
